text: This chapter built one real environment for one fictional company, start to finish — deployed it, secured and monitored it, troubleshot a cost spike in it, and now reviews how every chapter in this course actually showed up in that work. This isn't new material. It's the same seven chapters, seen as one connected deployment.

Governance came first: a resource group, tagged the moment it existed, before a single VM did. RBAC followed the same pattern — the ops team's Virtual Machine Contributor role was scoped to that one resource group, not the subscription. Compute and storage then matched their tiers to the actual workload: a modest Standard_B2s VM size, a Standard_LRS storage account, nothing oversized by default.

Networking's subnet split — web-subnet and app-subnet — only mattered because it gave the NSG rules something to attach to. app-nsg trusts traffic only from the web subnet's own address range, never the open internet. And underneath every one of those pieces sits the same az CLI from Chapter 6, which stopped being its own topic and became the thread running through all the others.

Every command across this chapter belongs to a different chapter's subject, and every one is still just an az command: group create for governance, role assignment create for identity, vm create for compute, storage account create for storage, nsg rule create for networking, metrics alert create and consumption budget create for monitoring and cost.

A CPU alert catches a performance problem by email instead of a complaint. A budget alert is what actually opened the Lesson 31 investigation — an automated threshold catching a real problem on day 19, not an invoice arriving thirty days later. That gap between deployed and operated is what Chapter 7 closed.

That's Microsoft Azure Administration, Compute & Storage, complete — course 3 of 15 in the Cloud Engineer to Cloud Architect path. Next up: AWS Cloud Infrastructure & Administration, where the same governance, compute, networking, and monitoring instincts get rebuilt on a different platform.
